justification: CB DCP 6.2 key site KS8 (212 South Terrace, 7 rules) was only in the may-apply box. Its address names one parcel (7,629 m2) that matches the plan's Figure 80 red key-site line at 0.992. Loaded and keyed before merge; live: the KS8 precinct serves 7 rules.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The KS8 keying rule is removed or keyed elsewhere.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before: KS8's 7 rows were unplaced (precinct layer, no key) and showed only in the may-apply box.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: CB DCP 2023 Ch 6.2 p182 text + Figure 80; NSW address register; build_site_boundaries proof (verbatim, named, neighbours, map IoU 0.992).

pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Of ~20 places tried only KS8 proved; others lack register addresses or a named LEP shape (recorded in the agent report).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One address-site entry, one keying rule, area row count trimmed 155 -> 148.

functions.if_none: zero matching rows means nothing is keyed or written

break_it.scenario: A neighbouring lot gets KS8's rules.
break_it.what_happens: A property next to the key site would be shown its rules.
break_it.how: Prover: no neighbour address inside; outline is the one parcel.

break_it.scenario: Other Bankstown houses lose KS8 in the box.

break_it.how: Rows keyed to a precinct the property is not in still show in the box (#1423).

break_it.what_happens: KS8 rules would reach nobody again.
